title: Shim a door's hinge jamb: drive two opposed tapered shims in from both wall faces until snug, not bowing it
instruction: Shim behind the door's hinge jamb at its hinge: push one wood shim in thin end first from each face of the wall until the pair is snug, without bowing the jamb.
context: Hanging prehung doors is everyday carpentry, and every one is set on shims. Before the hinge jamb is fastened to the stud, the gap behind it at each hinge is filled with a pair of tapered wood shims pushed in thin end first from the two faces of the wall, so their tapers cancel into a flat pack under the jamb. The pair must end snug, so the jamb cannot move when the hinge screw is driven, but no tighter: over-shimming bows the jamb and spoils the door's even 1/8-inch reveal, and a single shim or a lopsided pair leaves the jamb on one edge, so it twists when screwed. The gap differs at every hinge and door, and a millimetre of push thickens the pair by under 0.03 mm, so the stop is felt as the shims tighten, not measured. Carpenters (O*NET 47-2031, about 0.7 million US workers): "Install structures or fixtures, such as windows, frames, floorings, trim, or hardware, using carpenters' hand or power tools."
setup:
Millimetres. x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top; arm bases at y = +305 and -305.
Everything the shims touch is true size: the studs, the board, the jamb's cross-section, the gap and the shims. Only the wall's height and length and the jamb's length are cut.
Wall section (only its height and length cut), on a 6 mm steel base plate (x 150 to 330, y -90 to +90) fixed to the table: a doubled 2x4 SPF stud at the side of a rough opening, king stud x 184 to 222 and jack stud x 222 to 260, each 38 x 89 (y -44.5 to +44.5), 290 tall; 1/2 in (12.7) gypsum board on both faces (x 170 to 260, y +44.5 to +57.2 and -44.5 to -57.2), so the wall is 114.3 thick. The jack stud's face at x = 260 is the rough opening's side.
Hinge jamb: the middle-hinge part of an ordinary prehung interior door's hinge jamb, cut to 270 long and otherwise true size: primed finger-jointed pine, 17.5 thick (11/16 in, along x) and 115.9 wide (4-9/16 in, y -57.95 to +57.95, so its edges stand 0.8 proud of the wall faces), from z 16 to 286, parallel to the stud with its back face at x = 260 + g. A 3-1/2 in butt hinge's jamb leaf (89 x 32, satin nickel) is mortised in its front face with its centre at z = 130, knuckle at the right edge; the door is not hung. The rest of that jamb, already shimmed and tacked at its top and bottom hinges 1,486 apart, is replaced by a steel fixture (a rail under the section, a post and an arm over it, in front of the jamb) that carries the section on a slide toward and away from the stud with a 7 N per mm spring: the stiffness the whole jamb has at its middle hinge between those two tacked hinges (beam theory, README). At rest the gap is g.
Gap g: 4.0 to 6.35 (5/32 to 1/4 in), the same top to bottom, set per trial from its seed (README) and recorded.
Shims: two 8 in wood shims (Nelson type, kiln-dried cedar), each 203 long, 35 wide, tapering in thickness from 6.35 (1/4 in) at the butt to 0.8 (1/32 in) at the tip, one face flat, 10 g. Each stands on edge (width up) in a painted MDF holder block 50 (x) x 220 (y) x 30 tall with a slot along y 7 wide and 8 deep, its butt 10 proud of the block's outer end: holder centres (190, +205) and (190, -205); the left shim's tip points to -y with its flat face toward -x, the right shim's tip to +y with its flat face toward +x.
Both grippers start open at their ready poses. Friction (estimates within published values): wood on wood and wood on gypsum 0.4 static, 0.3 sliding.
scoring:
Measured once both grippers' centre points have been 30 mm or more from both shims and the jamb for 2 s, with the shims and jamb at rest (moved under 0.5 mm, 1 degree and 0.05 mm over the last second); before that the score is at most 0.25.
Terms. Gap: the space between the stud's face and the jamb's back. A shim is in the gap when its length runs across the wall (within 3 degrees), its middle is within 25 mm of the hinge's centre height, and its part between the jamb's edges lies between the stud and the jamb. Pair: one shim entered from each face of the wall, each thin end leading, both in the gap, their tapered faces on each other, overlapping by 70 mm or more, and the overlap covering the middle 40 mm of the jamb's width. Snug: a pair that bears on the jamb, leaving 0.05 mm or less of free space between the stud and the jamb at the jamb's centre line. Bow: how far the jamb now stands from where it started, away from the stud.
1.0: pair, snug, bow 0.4 mm (1/64 in) or less.
0.75: pair, snug, bow 0.4 to 0.8 mm (1/32 in).
0.5: pair, snug, bow 0.8 to 1.6 mm (1/16 in).
0.25: a snug pair that bows the jamb more than 1.6 mm; a pair that is not snug but leaves 1.5 mm or less of free space; or, with no pair, one shim alone in the gap at the hinge touching both the stud and the jamb.
0: anything else, including both shims still in or on their holders.
Which shim goes first, how far each goes and which hand does what are free.
Real trial: snug when a 0.05 mm feeler gauge will not enter between the pack and the jamb at the jamb's centre line; a dial indicator zeroed on the jamb's face at the start for bow; a tape for the overlap and the height.
reset_notes: Pull both shims out and stand them back in their holders (replace a shim whose tip is crushed or split). Set the next trial's gap with feeler gauges at the top and bottom of the jamb section, lock the fixture's stop, and zero the dial indicator.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Only lengths are cut; the jamb's cross-section, studs, board, gap and shims are true size. The 7 N/mm spring gives the 270 mm jamb section the stiffness the whole jamb has at its middle hinge between its tacked top and bottom hinges (beam theory, README); no twist joint, as no push the arm can make twists the jamb 0.15 degrees. Shims are rigid wedges of the real taper; real cedar crushes slightly. Friction 0.4 static, 0.3 sliding (published wood values). No nails are driven.
